clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old woman presented with acute painful worsening of chronic left thigh swelling present since childhood, associated with congenital capillary malformations (not initially appreciated on ED examination). Initial workup excluded deep vein thrombosis (Doppler ultrasound showed patent veins with soft tissue edema). MRI demonstrated subcutaneous and fascial edema with muscle hyperintensity but initially failed to identify arteriovenous malformations on radiologist interpretation. Over the subsequent 6 months, interventional radiology venogram revealed arteriovenous fistulas in the left thigh, establishing the high-flow component characteristic of Parkes-Weber syndrome (distinguishing it from Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome). Genetic analysis confirmed a pathogenic RASA1 variant (Chr5(GRCh37)g.86659154_86659154_86659158del), definitively confirming the diagnosis. Initial management consisted of supportive care with intravenous fluids and analgesics. Long-term follow-up was established for surveillance of potential complications including heart disease, limb ischemia, and aneurysms.
